req.title: Delete post
req.statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/delete issued by the post's author must delete the post row and redirect to /. I need to cover: (1) positive path — author deletes their own post, row gone, 302 to /; (2) negative path — non-author (other user) attempts delete, gets 403; (3) negative path — unauthenticated user attempts delete, gets 302 to login; (4) boundary — delete with non-existent id (id=0, one below the minimum valid id=1) returns 404; (5) state transition — after deletion the post is truly absent from the DB. These cover EP, NEG, BVA, STC, and DT heuristics and are designed to kill mutations on the status codes, the redirect target, the author-check condition, and the DELETE SQL.

tests.name: test_author_delete_post_redirects_to_index
preconditions: App initialised with test DB containing user id=1 (test/test) and post id=1 authored by user id=1
expected: Post id=1 no longer exists in the database
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login as author
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 302

# Delete post id=1
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Verify row is gone from DB
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
    assert row is None

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_delete_post_state_transition_absent_from_index
preconditions: App initialised with test DB containing post id=1 with title 'test title'
actions: GET / to confirm post is present before deletion
GET / to confirm post is absent after deletion
expected: Before delete: GET / returns 200 and contains b'test title'
After delete: GET / returns 200 and does NOT contain b'test title'
trace: R-FLASKR-021: row deleted — state transition from post-present to post-absent verified via index page
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 302

# State BEFORE: post visible on index
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'test title' in r.data

# Transition: delete
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# State AFTER: post absent from index
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'test title' not in r.data

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_delete_decision_table_author_vs_nonauthor
preconditions: Two users exist: test (author of post 1) and other (not author)
actions: Login as 'other', attempt POST /1/delete — expect 403, post still exists
Logout, login as 'test', attempt POST /1/delete — expect 302, post gone
expected: Non-author delete: status 403, post row still present
Author delete: status 302, Location '/', post row absent
trace: R-FLASKR-021: decision table covering author=False (403) and author=True (302+deleted)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Branch 1: non-author
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
assert r.status_code == 302
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 403
with app.app_context():
    row = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    assert row['id'] == 1

# Logout
client.get('/auth/logout')

# Branch 2: author
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 302
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
with app.app_context():
    row = get_db().execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
    assert row is None

os.unlink(path)
